questions.question:
Which of the following oxidation reactions are carried out by both \(\mathrm{K}_2 \mathrm{Cr}_2 \mathrm{O}_7\) and \(\mathrm{KMnO}_4\) in acidic medium?
A. \(\mathrm{I}^{-} \rightarrow \mathrm{I}_2\)
B. \(\mathrm{S}^{2-} \rightarrow \mathrm{S}\)
C. \(\mathrm{Fe}^{2+} \rightarrow \mathrm{Fe}^{3+}\)
D. \(\mathrm{I}^{-} \rightarrow \mathrm{IO}_3^{-}\)
E. \(\mathrm{S}_2 \mathrm{O}_3^{2-} \rightarrow \mathrm{SO}_4^{2-}\)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
1. B, C and D only
2. A, D and E only
3. A, B and C only
4. C, D and E only
questions.explanation:
Hint:Both\(\mathrm{K}_2 \mathrm{Cr}_2 \mathrm{O}_7\) and\(\mathrm{KMnO}_4\) are strong oxidizing agents in an acidic medium. Explanation: In an acidic medium, both K₂Cr₂O₇ and KMnO₄ act as oxidizing agents, but KMnO₄ is generally a stronger oxidizing agent than K₂Cr₂O₇. KMnO₄ can oxidize a wider range of substances and is more reactive in acidic conditions. In an acidic medium, both can convert an anion to a neutral molecule and a cation to the next higher oxidation state. The given reactions can take place in the following medium: \(\mathrm{I}^{-} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{H}^{+}} \mathrm{I}_2\)\(\mathrm{I}^{-} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{OH}^{-}} \mathrm{IO}_3^{-}\) \(\mathrm{S}^{-2} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{H}^{+}} \mathrm{S}\)\(\mathrm{S}_2 \mathrm{O}_3^{2-} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{OH}^{-}} \mathrm{SO}_4^{2-}\) \(\mathrm{Fe}^{+2}\ \xrightarrow{\mathrm{H}^{+}}\ \mathrm{Fe}^{+3}\) \(\mathrm{S}_2 \mathrm{O}_3^{2-} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{H}^{+}} \mathrm{S} \downarrow+\mathrm{SO}_4^{2-} \) Hence, option 3is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements are true?
(i)The chromate ion is square planar.
(ii)The green manganate ion is diamagnetic.
(iii)Dichromate can be prepared using chromate.
(iv) Dark green \(\text{KMnO}_4\) disproportionates in acidic and neutral mediums.
(v)For d-block elements, ionic character decreases for increasing oxidation numbers of the metal in oxides.
1. (i) and (ii)
2. (iii) and (iv)
3. (i) and (iv)
4. (iii) and (v)
questions.explanation:
Hint: Manganate ion is paramagnetic with one unpaired\(\text{e}^-\)but the permanganate is diamagnetic.(i) Chromate ion is square planar. False. The chromate ion (CrO₄²⁻) has Cr in +6 oxidation state with d⁰ configuration. It has tetrahedral geometry (sp³ hybridization), not square planar. Square planar geometry is typical for d⁸ metals (like Ni²⁺, Pd²⁺, Pt²⁺) in coordination number 4. (ii) Green manganate ion is diamagnetic. False. The green manganate ion is MnO₄²⁻ (Mn in +6 oxidation state). Mn⁶⁺ has electron configuration [Ar] 3d¹. It has one unpaired electron, so it is paramagnetic, not diamagnetic. (iii) Dichromate can be prepared using chromate. True. Yes, dichromate (Cr₂O₇²⁻) is prepared from chromate (CrO₄²⁻) in acidic medium: 2CrO₄²⁻ + 2H⁺ ⇌ Cr₂O₇²⁻ + H₂O This is a standard equilibrium reaction. In acidic conditions, chromate converts to dichromate (orange). (iv) Dark green KMnO₄ disproportionate in acidic medium and neutral medium. False. KMnO₄ is actually purple (not dark green). * Dark green color is for manganate ion (MnO₄²⁻), not KMnO₄. * KMnO₄ (MnO₄⁻, Mn⁷⁺) undergoes disproportionation in strongly alkaline medium (not acidic or neutral). In acidic medium it is reduced to Mn²⁺, and in neutral/weakly alkaline to MnO₂. Hence, both the color description and the medium are incorrect. (v) For d-block elements, ionic character decreases for increasing oxidation no. of the metal in oxides. True. This follows Fajans' rules. As the oxidation number (charge) of the metal ion increases, its polarizing power increases. This increases covalent character and decreases ionic character in the oxides. Example: * MnO (Mn²⁺) → more ionic * Mn₂O₇ (Mn⁷⁺) → highly covalent (acidic oxide) Therefore, (iii) and (v) are correct.

questions.chapter: The d and f Block Elements
questions.question:
In context with the transition elements, which of the following statements is incorrect?

1.In addition to the normal oxidation state, the zero oxidation state is also shown by these elements in complexes.
2.In the highest oxidation states, the transition metal shows basic character and forms cationic complexes.
3.In the highest oxidation states of the first five transition elements (Sc to Mn), all the 4s and 3d electrons are used for bonding.
4.Once the d5 configuration is exceeded, the tendency to involve all the 3d electrons in bonding decreases.
questions.explanation:
Hint: As the oxidation state increases, acidic character increases. Explanation: (1) The first statement is correct. The d-block element shows a zero oxidation state in the complexes, like\(Ni(CO)_{4}\). This is possible because such ligands can stabilize the metal atom by back-donation of electron density, allowing the metal to retain all its valence electrons. (2) The second statement is wrong because as the oxidation state increases, the acidic character increases, not the basic character. Transition metals in their highest oxidation states (e.g., Cr(VI), Mn(VII), Os(VIII)) act as Lewis acids (electron acceptors), not bases. High oxidation states (+3 to +7) typically form anionic oxo-complexes (e.g., [MnO₄]⁻, [CrO₄]²⁻) or neutral oxides (e.g., OsO₄), not cationic complexes. (3) The third statement is also correct because the first five transition elements (Sc to Mn), show a maximum oxidation state. Like Cr shows up to +6 and Mn shows up to +7. All electrons in 3d and 4s orbitals in the case of Sc to Mn take part in bonding. (4) The fourth statement is correct. Once the d5 configuration is exceeded, the tendency to involve all the 3d electrons in bonding decreases because the pairing of electrons takes place and fewer electrons are left for bonding. Hence, option 2 is the correct answer.
